The trip record's contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 against an empty messages array (source EV-CHAT-05053) while listing two calls (12:17:55 and 12:19:40). One limb of a conjunctive obligation is not the obligation, and POL-NS-23 states in terms that where either is missing 'the fee is voided and the rider is not charged'. The 5.00 SGD fee must therefore be voided.

The chat log independently confirms the omission rather than merely failing to record a message: it holds exactly one entry and that entry is the rider's own — 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50 and delivered at 12:21:53 — 40 seconds AFTER the driver cancelled at 12:21:10. Every driver-side entry in the log is absent, and none exists in the window between auto-arrival at 12:15:30 and cancellation at 12:21:10. There is no message to weigh in the driver's favour.

POL-NS-23 places the obligation on the driver's acts — one message and one call — not on the rider's responsiveness: an unanswered call is precisely the situation in which the message limb does its work, by putting in writing where the driver is waiting.
